# Premise falsified — the 1M-file cap this task was filed on has been resolved; parking at `on_hold`

Posted by the `/issue 2286` session (2026-08-22). #2286, #2287 and **#2300** are
three independent filings of the SAME condition on 2026-08-14 (from #2254, #2225
and #2094 respectively). The condition is gone. This note records the evidence so
no further session re-derives it; the systemic fix for the duplication itself is
**#2390**.

## This task's Goal, and its status

> "Restore the ability to upload NEW files to the project data repo
> `superkaiba1/explore-persona-space-data`, and document the routing so no future
> round silently loses artifacts."

Both halves are **DONE**, by two tasks that landed on `origin/main` after this one
was filed. Verified at blob level by this session, not taken from reports.

**Upload capability restored — #2332** (merge `87640d1a1b`, an ancestor of
`origin/main`) executed the repack on 2026-08-16/17: canonical repo **938,366 →
445,580 files, 492,786 slots freed**, every prefix with
`kept_stale=0, kept_new=0`. Independently measured on 2026-08-19 by #2321 (three
agreeing reads): **454,804 / 1,000,000 — 545,196 slots free.** The packed-path
reader `src/explore_persona_space/orchestrate/packed_prefix.py` is present on
`origin/main` and hooked at the central `hub.py` staging seam, so repacked
prefixes still resolve for consumers — the "no future round silently loses
artifacts" half of the Goal.

**Routing documented and wired — #2304** (squash `52ee7c026a`, PR #1979, an
ancestor of `origin/main`) extended the #1108 reactive file-count overflow
fallback to `repo_type == "dataset"` AND to bulk `upload_folder` commits. Both
gaps mattered: the old guard admitted only `model`, and the fallback lived only in
`_upload`, which a bulk push never enters. On `origin/main` a single shared
`_filecount_overflow_retry` helper is called from both `_upload` and
`_upload_folder_filtered`, gated at `hub.py:1451` on
`repo_type in ("model", "dataset")`. `.claude/rules/upload-policy.md` gained the
data-repo file-count clause (+77 lines), and `preflight.py:1876` gained the
WARN-only early-warning `check_hf_filecount_sentinel`.

**Behavioral confirmation:** a scan of every `tasks/*/*/events.jsonl` for the
Hub's verbatim file-count rejection text with `ts >= 2026-08-17` returns **zero
hits** — five days of heavy fleet uploading with no recurrence. The 08-14 filings
were made during a burst of them.

## Disposition

`on_hold` — excluded from auto-dispatch and from the active proposed queue, still
revivable. This task looks fully superseded with no residue (unlike #2287, whose
scope item 4 leaves a small typed-exception judgement call), so archival is very
likely correct — but closing someone else's task is Thomas's call, not an
autonomous session's. Close with `task.py set-status 2300 archived`; revive with
`task.py set-status 2300 proposed`.

Why parked rather than left in `proposed`: this task is auto-dispatchable, and the
`/issue 2286` session that wrote this note was itself a watcher
`proposed-infra-sweep` dispatch. Left in `proposed`, #2300 draws a full session
that re-derives this investigation against a five-day-dead premise. Nothing about
the task was edited — body, tags and `parent_id: 2094` are untouched.

Superseded premise: the 1M-file cap was resolved by tasks 2304 (dataset+bulk overflow routing) and 2332 (492,786 slots reclaimed; repo now 454,804/1,000,000). Parked out of the auto-dispatch queue by the /issue 2286 session; evidence in the epm:progress note of 2026-08-22. No residue identified; archival is likely correct but is Thomas's call. Revivable via task.py set-status 2300 proposed.
